svg.text: Глава 9 · Технология первичных сетей DWDM
Олифер, 7-е изд. · RAG p0268:c01–p0281:c01 · PDF 268–281 · printed 267–280
1 · DWDM = many spectral channels in one fiber
Each modulated optical channel occupies a finite frequency spectrum
“Wavelength” refers to the central wavelength of that spectral channel
Multiplexing is a form of FDM implemented in optical domain
Dispersion · interference · diffraction · reflection enable optical devices
These physical effects can be either impairments or useful mechanisms depending on design
2 · Frequency-grid engineering
CWDM → coarse spacing · DWDM → dense spacing
Fixed grid → equal slots around defined center frequencies
Flexible grid → slot widths vary by required bandwidth
Narrow spacing improves spectral efficiency but increases filtering/modulation requirements
Exact grid numbers remain source/standard-revision snapshots
3 · Terminal line components
Transponder → client wavelength ↔ assigned DWDM wavelength via O-E-O
Optical M/D → combine/split coloured channels into/from colourless composite
Thin-film filters → simple wavelength selection, cumulative attenuation limits scaling
Diffraction/waveguide structures → source presents better scaling to many wavelengths
OADM → fixed wavelength add/drop without changing remaining channel set
Same wavelength cannot collide on one composite output
4 · Reach: power and dispersion
EDFA → erbium-doped optical amplification around source-described band
Raman → distributed optical amplification example with broader source-described band
Amplifier boosts optical signal; regenerator restores digital waveform/timing
Chromatic and polarization-mode dispersion can constrain reach/rate
Compensation may be fiber/device based or receiver-DSP based
Exact power/gain/dispersion budget requires system-specific data
5 · Mesh and optical cross-connect
OXC → arbitrary spectral-channel switching among network directions
Optoelectronic OXC → intermediate electrical processing
Photonic OXC / lambda router → fully optical switching path
Number of line “directions” describes immediate optical adjacency
Mesh improves path flexibility and fault-tolerance options
6 · ROADM + WSS
ROADM → remotely modify optical switching state
WSS → choose required wavelength from each ingress composite and combine output
Power splitter distributes incoming composites to WSS blocks
MEMS mirrors are one source-described physical switching implementation
Reconfigurable ≠ automatically colorless and directionless
Operational reading rule
Trace wavelength continuity and optical resource state first: transponder → grid slot → add/drop → amplifier/dispersion → WSS/ROADM → destination.
Do not confuse optical amplifier with regenerator; do not assume every ROADM is colorless/directionless.
No executable CLI is supplied by the chapter.
Questions to Part II start at p0282:c01 · reading state unchanged · source findings recorded separately.
